title: Import records: never swallow a failure, and log it once

blocks.text: Two anti-patterns hide or blur a failure: *swallowing* it in an empty `catch`, and *logging and rethrowing* it so that every layer logs it again. Log a failure once, where it is finally handled. Write `Importer(List<String> log)`:

items: `int importAll(List<String> records) throws ImportException` parses every record as an `int` and returns their sum. At the first record that is not an integer it throws `ImportException("Bad record at line <n>: <record>")` (lines count from 1). This layer does **not** log.
`int importOrZero(List<String> records)` is the handler: it returns `importAll(records)`, or, when that throws, appends `"import failed: " + message` to the log and returns `0`.

rows: `["import failed: Bad record at line 2: x"]`

blocks.text: `ImportException` is given. Whoever investigates the failure later wants to see the parse error behind it too.

cases.says: Good records are summed by both methods, and nothing is logged.
A bad record makes importAll throw ImportException naming its line, and importOrZero return 0.
The handler logs the failure it handles; an empty catch would hide it.
Only the handler logs: the layer that throws does not log and rethrow, so the failure appears once.
The NumberFormatException is kept as the cause of the ImportException.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Logging and rethrowing makes every layer log the same failure; log it once, where it is handled.
An empty catch block hides a failure; handle it, rethrow it, or at least log it.
Throw early where the input is checked, catch late where the caller can act.
